diagnosis: The scenario passed 3 of 4 rollouts, meeting the min_pass_required threshold of 3, but rollout 3 failed due to a turn-cap auto-fail. The single failing rollout (rollout 3) hit the turn cap at 10 turns without settling. The transcript shows a pacing/structural problem: turns 1-6 were consumed by conversational pleasantries and coordination overhead (A3 saying 'I'll go first', A2 saying 'I'll hold my findings', A2 repeating readiness at turn 6) before A3 finally revealed PF2 at turn 7. By turn 9 (the last turn before the cap), A1 had acknowledged PF2 and invited A2 to share, but A2 (owner of PF1) never got a turn to reveal PF1 before the cap was hit. Only PF2 was revealed; PF1 was never revealed. No content or provenance checks ran because the rollout never settled. This is a pacing problem: the 10-turn cap is too low for a 3-agent scenario where pleasantries and turn-taking coordination consume 6+ turns before the first reveal, leaving insufficient turns for the second fact-holder (A2) to reveal and the settler (A1) to settle. The three passing rollouts (0, 1, 2) all settled in 5-6 turns, but rollout 3's conversational overhead pushed it past the cap. No content checks, provenance checks, or specific fact IDs failed in any settled rollout — all failures are attributable solely to the turn-cap auto-fail in rollout 3.
